MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Sample Type: Fetal sample
Sample ID: [redacted ID]
Referring Clinician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

TEST PERFORMED
Multiplex Ligation-dependent Probe Amplification (MLPA) - Subtelomeric Screen
Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) - Aneuploidy Screen

METHODOLOGY
MLPA Analysis:
DNA was extracted from the fetal sample using standard protocols. MLPA was performed using SALSA MLPA probemix P036 and P070 (MRC-Holland) containing probes for all subtelomeric regions. The analysis includes probes targeting the p and q arms of all chromosomes (1-22, X and Y). Fragment analysis was performed on an ABI 3730xl Genetic Analyzer. Data was analyzed using Coffalyser.Net software with normalization against reference samples.

QF-PCR Analysis:
Quantitative Fluorescence-PCR was performed for rapid aneuploidy detection using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y. The following markers were analyzed:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742
- Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S858
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1446
- Sex chromosomes: AMELX/Y, SRY, XHPRT, X22

PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis on an ABI 3730xl Genetic Analyzer.

RESULTS

MLPA SUBTELOMERIC ANALYSIS:
Result: No abnormality detected

All subtelomeric regions showed normal copy number (ratio 0.85-1.15) when compared to reference samples. No evidence of subtelomeric deletions or duplications was identified.

Detailed probe ratios:
- All p-arm subtelomeres: Normal (ratios 0.92-1.08)
- All q-arm subtelomeres: Normal (ratios 0.89-1.11)
- Internal control probes: Normal

QF-PCR ANEUPLOIDY SCREEN:
Result: No aneuploidy detected

Chromosome 13: Biallelic pattern consistent with disomy
Chromosome 18: Biallelic pattern consistent with disomy
Chromosome 21: Biallelic pattern consistent with disomy
Sex chromosomes: Pattern consistent with male karyotype (XY)
- AMELX/Y: Two peaks detected (X and Y specific)
- SRY: Present
- X-linked markers: Single allele pattern

Triploidy assessment: Diallelic ratios within normal range (1:1), excluding triploidy

INTERPRETATION
The combined MLPA and QF-PCR analyses have excluded:
1. Whole chromosome aneuploidy for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y
2. Subtelomeric imbalances for all chromosomes
3. Triploidy

The results are consistent with a male sex chromosome complement (XY).

LIMITATIONS
- This test does not detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Small deletions/duplications (<100kb) in non-subtelomeric regions will not be detected
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be reliably detected
- QF-PCR is limited to detection of aneuploidy for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y only
- Maternal cell contamination cannot be completely excluded

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
These results have excluded the most common chromosomal causes of developmental abnormalities including whole chromosome aneuploidy, subtelomeric imbalances, and triploidy. The male sex chromosome complement has been confirmed. However, this testing does not exclude all genetic causes of fetal abnormalities.

Authorized by: Dr. [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Date: [redacted date]
